drivingQuestion: Why may one draw lots with family but not with others?
outcomeNote: Answered by Shmuel's dictum, which continues in the next unit

segments.he: מֵפִיס אָדָם עִם בָּנָיו וְכוּ׳. עִם בָּנָיו וְעִם בְּנֵי בֵיתוֹ אִין, וְעִם אַחֵר — לָא. מַאי טַעְמָא? כִּדְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל. דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: בְּנֵי חֲבוּרָה הַמַּקְפִּידִין זֶה עַל זֶה — עוֹבְרִין מִשּׁוּם מִדָּה וּמִשּׁוּם מִשְׁקָל וּמִשּׁוּם מִנְיָן, וּמִשּׁוּם לוֹוִין וּפוֹרְעִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
segments.en: We learned in the mishna that «a person may draw lots with one’s children» and family members at the table on Shabbat to see who will receive which meal portion. The Gemara infers: «With one’s children and family members, yes,» it is permitted, «but with another» person it is «not. What is the reason» for this? The Gemara explains that it is «as Rav Yehuda» said that «Shmuel said,» for «Rav Yehuda said» that «Shmuel said: Members of a group» who are eating together on Shabbat or on a Festival and «who are particular with each other» that no one receive a larger portion than anyone else «are in violation of» the prohibitions of «measuring, and weighing, and counting» merchandise on Shabbat or a Festival, «and» they are also in violation «of» the prohibition against «lending and repaying on a Festival.»
